details: The Bank of Russia has proposed new regulations that would cap annual cryptocurrency purchases for non-qualified retail investors at 300,000 rubles (approximately $3,600 USD) per intermediary. Initially, only Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Tether's USDT would be approved for public trading. Qualified investors would have broader access without limits after passing a risk test. These rules are part of a framework to regulate domestic trading, separate from cross-border crypto use for exporters and importers.
title: Russia Limits Retail Crypto Buys to ₽300,000 Annually

details: Coinbase has secured a Financial Services Permission (FSP) from the Financial Services Regulatory Authority (FSRA) of Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) to establish an international tokenization hub. This license allows Coinbase to arrange investment deals and provide custody services for tokenized securities, aiming to democratize access to global capital markets. The initiative highlights the UAE's progressive regulatory environment for blockchain and tokenized assets.
title: Coinbase Launches Tokenization Hub in Abu Dhabi

details: Tether, the issuer of the USDT stablecoin, announced the successful completion of its first full independent financial audit for the year ended December 31, 2025, conducted by KPMG U.S. KPMG issued an unqualified opinion, confirming that Tether's reserves exceeded its liabilities by $6.814 billion at the end of 2025. The audit involved a thorough examination of assets, transactions, systems, and even a physical count of gold bars held in reserve.
title: Tether Receives Unqualified Audit Opinion from KPMG

details: The UK's Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) is engaged in settlement discussions with cryptocurrency exchange HTX (formerly Huobi) regarding allegations of unlawfully promoting crypto services to British consumers. London's High Court has paused legal proceedings until late August to allow for negotiations. This marks the FCA's first enforcement action against a crypto exchange specifically for marketing violations.
title: UK Regulator Negotiates with HTX on Illegal Crypto Ads

details: Spanish banking group BBVA has received regulatory approval to offer Bitcoin and Ethereum trading services to its customers in Spain. This enables clients to buy, sell, and manage cryptocurrency transactions directly through the bank's mobile application. This development follows BBVA's earlier similar ventures in other markets and aligns with the evolving regulatory landscape, including the implementation of MiCA in the European Union.
title: BBVA Gets Green Light for Bitcoin & Ethereum Trading in Spain

details: Geopolitical tensions and the weaponization of economic relations are profoundly challenging the global economic equilibrium. Maritime disruptions in crucial chokepoints like the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea, alongside fierce competition over critical mineral supply chains, are systematically weaponizing geography. This leads to increased uncertainty about future trade architectures and forces companies to build costly "just-in-case" supply chain redundancies.
title: Global Economy Faces Uncertainty Amid Geopolitical Tensions & Trade Fragmentation
